summary: Production Library Import System v2.0 fully verified end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest tests pass covering template v2.0 shape (unit_aliases, import_features, valid_measurement_units), unit alias mapping (SQ→SF, SQFT→SF, LUMP SUM→LS), auto-created lookup detection (Knowledge Domains + Service Categories), commit duplicate strategies (skip creates fresh + skips + updates), auto-creation of missing domains/categories on commit, unit_conversions counter, invalid duplicate_strategy → 400, and auth guards on both endpoints. Frontend: Import Wizard at /app/production-library?tab=import loads with the correct v2.0 step indicator (Initialize → Template → Upload → Validate → Import). Preview step surfaces validation_groups (Auto-Created Lookups, Unit Conversions with SQ→SF visualization, Warnings with duplicate messaging), shows Duplicate Handling section with Skip/Update/Replace options, and the final Import Summary page displays imported/updated/skipped/warnings + unit conversions + Company Brain learning callout. Full happy-path import completed in ~0.89s.

minor.issue: LookupResolver.resolve_domain / resolve_category calls value.strip().title() to build canonical names. Titlecasing mangles mixed-case tokens (e.g. 'TestV2 Domain' becomes 'Testv2 Domain', 'DHW' becomes 'Dhw'). Consider preserving the original casing verbatim or normalising via a smarter case rule.

In the row loop `for i, row in enumerate(reader, 1)`, the code later writes `critical = [i for i in issues if i.severity == ValidationSeverity.CRITICAL]` reusing `i` as the comprehension variable. Safe in Python 3 but confusing. Rename the comprehension variable (e.g. `iss`) to avoid shadowing.

The function is not truly transactional. If an item POST fails mid-loop, previously created domains/categories/items remain committed. Documentation calls this 'transactional' but it is best-effort per-row. Either wrap in a Supabase RPC/transaction or update docs.

action_items: OPTIONAL: In services/import_engine.py LookupResolver.resolve_domain/resolve_category, drop the value.strip().title() call or replace with a smarter titlecaser that preserves acronyms/mixed case (currently 'TestV2 Domain' becomes 'Testv2 Domain').
OPTIONAL: In routes/production_library.py commit_import inner loop, rename the list-comprehension variable that shadows the outer `i` (row index) — pure readability fix.

OPTIONAL: The commit endpoint claims transactional but performs per-row REST writes. If a mid-loop failure happens, previously created domains/categories/items are not rolled back. Either implement a Supabase RPC/DB transaction or soften the wording in the docstring.

OPTIONAL: routes/production_library.py is 2240 lines and ImportWizard.jsx is 1327 lines — both far above the 700-line guideline. Consider extracting the import subsystem into its own router module (e.g. routes/production_library_import.py) and splitting the wizard into per-step components.
OPTIONAL: The commit endpoint uses .json()[0] on the first POST response without guarding against empty lists; a race where 201 returns [] would raise IndexError. Same for domain/category creation.

OPTIONAL: Repeated test runs accumulate `TestV2 …` Knowledge Domains and Service Categories in the org (2 new domains/categories per full run). Add a tear-down (archive by name prefix) or an admin cleanup endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/production_library.py exceeds 2200 lines; the import subsystem (~700 LOC) should live in its own module. This hurts maintainability and increases risk of regressions across unrelated CRUD endpoints.

commit endpoint's transactional claim is aspirational — no DB transaction is opened, so partial failures leave orphan created lookups (domains/categories) and orphan production_items. Either use a Postgres function/RPC or document as best-effort with cleanup.

services/import_engine.py LookupResolver.resolve_domain returns synthetic ids of the form `pending:<name_lower>`. During PHASE 2 re-resolve, the code strips the 'pending:' prefix from category ids and passes the raw lowercase key back into resolve_category. This works because the resolver stores names in lowercase-keys, but it is fragile if the key ever contains characters that title-cased differently between phases.
ImportWizard.jsx (1327 lines) mixes fetching, orchestration, and 5 sub-step components in a single file. Extract the sub-step components + move the API calls into a dedicated hook for testability.

MeasurementUnitAliasMapper's alias table is defined as a class-level dict. Adding a new alias currently requires editing source; consider promoting the alias table to a DB-backed lookup so admins can curate aliases without deploys.

The commit endpoint accepts both `duplicate_strategy` and the deprecated `update_existing`; if a caller passes update_existing=true AND duplicate_strategy='replace', the code silently keeps 'replace' — worth logging a deprecation warning and rejecting the conflict.
resolve_domain / resolve_category use .title() to canonicalise names. This corrupts mixed-case tokens ('DHW' → 'Dhw', 'TestV2' → 'Testv2'). Consider preserving user input verbatim on first creation.
seed_data_creation: During testing the following rows were persisted to Two Fungis Finishing org (Supabase): production_items TESTV2-DUP-{RUN_ID}, TESTV2-AUTO-{RUN_ID}, TESTV2-UC-{RUN_ID}, TESTV2-UI-NEW (all with 'TESTV2-' prefix); a handful of TestV2 Domain/Cat lookup rows also created via auto-create. Library counts grew from 21/13/60 to 23/15/66. Prefix 'TESTV2-' can be used for future teardown queries.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Import Wizard requires the Production Library to be initialized in the target org — Two Fungis Finishing org (a0000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002) is already seeded with the base Finish Carpentry / Doors & Hardware domains, so tests can rely on 'Finish Carpentry' being an existing (non-auto-created) domain. To force an 'auto-create' scenario, use a unique domain string like 'TestV2 Domain <uuid>'. Note: the backend title-cases new domain/category names, so match case-insensitively in assertions. Repeated test runs continue to accumulate TESTV2-* rows and TestV2 * lookups; there is no cleanup endpoint. The commit endpoint is not truly transactional (per-row REST writes) even though the docstring calls it 'transactional'.
